ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.34  
DESCRIPTION: [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L270) does not validate `CapabilityFingerprint`, while [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L413) assumes the normalised vector stays within `[0,1]` and documents scores in `[0,1]`. That contract is false as implemented. I verified this by constructing `CapabilityFingerprint(D_decay=-1.0, v_bar=nan, A=2.0, C=-0.5)`: `assign()` produced capability scores above `1.0` (`PM=1.1`, `COL=1.2`, `PAR=1.5`) and promoted the malformed model to `PM`.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add `CapabilityFingerprint.__post_init__` to enforce finiteness and schema bounds before scoring. Reject `NaN`/`inf` and out-of-range values explicitly, then add regression tests that invalid fingerprints raise.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_R1_F011  
SEVERITY: 0.76  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.71  
DESCRIPTION: Cross-component, unverified from Role Assignment alone: [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L621) only penalises a model when `record_failure()` is called, but [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L4306) records failures only for models present in `responses`. If an active model returns no `ModelResponse` object at all, its role-assignment failure rate stays `0.0` and it remains eligible for future work. I reproduced this through `DynamicManager.process_round()`: omitting `m3` from `responses` left `phi_hist(m3)=0.0` and `m3` still active.  
PROPOSED_FIX: At the manager/failure boundary, synthesise an explicit failure for every active model missing from `responses` and feed that into `RoleAssignment.record_failure`. If “missing response” is intended to be distinct from `EMPTY`/`TIMEOUT`, model it as its own typed failure and test the end-to-end path.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

DESCRIPTION: [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L103) exposes `theta_col` as a COL-selection threshold, but [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L488) and [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L597) never read it. I verified this by setting `theta_col=0.99`; `assign()` still created a `COL` whose score was only `0.1556`. This is a silent API-contract break: callers can set a documented control that has no effect.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either implement threshold semantics in both `assign()` and `reassign()` or remove `theta_col` from `DynamicManagementConfig` and its documentation. Add a regression test either way.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_R1_F013  
SEVERITY: 0.64  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63  
DESCRIPTION: [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L516) accepts `round_idx` “for failure history”, but the method never uses it, and [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L621) stores history as a plain `List[bool]`. So `phi_hist` is not actually round-indexed: duplicate writes in one round count as multiple rounds, and skipped writes erase rounds from the denominator. I verified this by calling `record_failure('m2', True)` twice in succession and observing history `[True, True]` with rate `1.0`.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Store failure history by round, change the API to `record_failure(model_id, round_idx, failed)`, reject duplicate writes for the same round, and compute `phi_hist` from an explicit round window.  
VERIFIED: TRUE
